newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle weaker and near lows.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle weaker and near lows.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower after a dull Friday session that brought the spot July contract closer to its downside target of 70.00 cents.
July ended down 0.85 cent at 72.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.10 to 72.30 cents. September closed 0.55 lower at 75.50 cents.
The rest of the board finished 0.70 lower to 0.85 higher.

Total open interest climbed to record levels this week as the speculators added to their net short position. The rise in liquidity amid declining prices suggested to some technical analysts that further weakness may be in store.
Open interest stood at 32,229 lots as of Thursday, down 3,096 lots from the previous session.
Other analysts said that other indicators suggest that a bottom is already in place.
But the fundamental situation continues to weigh on the market. Supplies remain at a projected 224.2 million 90-lb boxes, while demand for orange juice has yet to pick up.

"We see little change in the demand scenario as retail prices remain stubbornly high compared to the market, and it seems like this is not apt to change any time soon," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said in a weekly citrus comment.

Indeed, weekly movement of juice was only 4,798,750 gallons for the week ended June 21, compared with 4,145,695 gallons the previous week, the Florida Citrus Processors' Association, said on Thursday.
An estimated 4,000 lots changed hands on the day, versus Thursday's official 5,068 lots.
